newsitem.title: MACAU: U.S. to keep separate relationship with Macau-envoy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to keep separate relationship with Macau-envoy.

text.p: A senior United States envoy said on Thursday that Washington expected to maintain a separate relationship with Macau after the Portuguese-run territory reverts to Chinese rule in 1999.
Richard Boucher, the U.S. consul-general to Hong Kong and Macau, said his government expected "to maintain a distinct and autonomous relationship with Macau".
Boucher was speaking in the territory on the outlook for United States-Macau relations.
Portuguese-run Macau will revert to Chinese administration in December 1999, some two and a half years after the nearby British colony of Hong Kong returns to Beijing.
Boucher also reiterated Washington's plea to Macau to crack down on piracy and violators of intellectual property rights.
"A strong intellectual property rights regime is essential to Macau's efforts to attract foreign investment and to develop high technology industry and services," Boucher said.

The envoy, who said Macau's competitive edge was its lower rents compared to Hong Kong, its airport and its warehouses, said the United States absorbed 40 percent of Macau's total export value and about half its textile and garment exports in 1996.
